Cyril Ramaphosa

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
He was the man chosen but Mandela to lead the country after Mandela's exit but this was a dream deferred now 28 years later as Cyril Ramaphosa is about to step into the shoes of his mentor is history finally on his side. A profile of Cyril Ramaphosa has his life been all about preparing for this moment. We look back at various crucial times in Ramahosa's life in politics in business and how this has moulded the man. Through interviews we try and deepen our insight....Is history finally on his side.

After todays news of Zumas recall what does that mean fro Cyril Ramaphosa, has his negotiating tactics proved successful of is he as one analyst critics not enough of a muscleman. How has Cyrils background in business and commerce affected the president he will become. He vowed to stop corruption and state capture how will that pan out. We take a look at Cyril Ramaphosa in light of the background he has had.



A profile of Cyril Ramaphosa has his life been all about preparing for this moment. We look back at various crucial times in Ramahosa's life in politics in business and how this has moulded the man. Through interviews we try and deepen our insight....Is history finally on his side.

Script:


Link
What happens to a dream deferred? When NM greeted the world after 27 years of imprisonment it was Cyril Ramphosa, who stood beside him holding the mike …it would be 28 years before he would take to the same stage to address the country as the ANC President it had been a long long wait can he step up to the plate.

V/O 6 sec
At 66 years old, this week, Matemela Cyril Ramaphosa achieved his ambition to lead South Africa.

Frank: I think it’s good to be President isn’t it but it’s a daunting task

V/O 8 sec
Reverend Frank Chikane and Cyril go back a long way, growing up in Soweto they were both students together and friends.

Rev. Frank Chikane

Frank: There was a tradition in Soweto of youth groups in late 60’s and the 70’s …highly spiritual person in his youth…Then we went to to the University. He became chair of the Students Christian Movement. During the Student Christian Movement days. I took him as one of the best managers and administrators he was able to manage an organization.

Link
!985 First General Sect of Nat UM It was his Grand Entry on to the National Stage within 2 years he and his comrades managed to organise the biggest strike the country has ever seen.

Up Sound James Motlatsi: “ On the 9th August 1987 Brought the country to its knees”

James Motlatsi

V/O
As President of NUM Dr James Motlatsi was co organiser of the strike … Cyril a labour lawyer from Soweto; James working as a miner underground with only a Std 6… they came from different worlds

James: As a mine worker coming from the rural areas meeting with somebody who was coming from a township who had no knowledge whatsoever about the mining industry to say he was interested about organising the mineworkers. I didn’t really accept it easily because of so many companies particularly companies who lied to the mineworkers if you can join us we will do AB and C, and after that ran away with the mineworkers money.

V/O
Cyril didn’t steal the mine worker’s money but built up what was to become the most powerful union in the country… …
For Political Analyst Prof Mcebisi Ndletyana it was Cyril’s refusal to concede to the Mine management in the strike that illustrated his future success in negotiation.

Prof Mcebisi Ndletyana:
Political Analyst

It took a strike, It was a very protracted strike because the mining sector and government were unwilling to concede he was not willing to blink first so that told you of someone who can use brinkmanship quiet effectively and interestingly that experience proved to be quiet useful for the negotiations in the early 1990’s, if you read Roelf Meyer accounts for that period he says the difference between the two negotiating teams theirs and the ANC was Cyril Ramaphosa because Cyril could press them could push them.

Link
Ramaphosa has quiet a reputation as a formidable negotiator he is known as a consensus builder someone who is able to mend bridges to bring all sides but the one constant against him is he does not seem to have the muscle to bring all sides well this week he rose to the fore and how

V/O 6 sec
While South African’s became impatient for the recall or resignation of Zuma..Ramaphosa played a waiting game

Ray: The longer Ramaphosa left Zuma in the Union Buildings the more that support has drifted in his direction.

V/O
Journalist, Ray Hartley, wrote ‘The Man who would be King’ a biography of Ramaphosa
Ray Hartley
Author: The man who would be king.

Bongani: And also he didn’t allow Zuma to do what he does does best, play the victim although he did that at the very end.
Ray: Exactly although it wasn’t convincing because Ramaphosa has not confronted him has not insulted him, has not publically called for his departure Zuma would have thrived on being attacked and aggressively pushed out of power and he would have used that to mobilise his faction.

V/O 12 sec
Ramaphosa was Mandela’s choice as to become his successor as the nation’s leader…but ANC’s exile fraternity pressed successfully for one of their own Thabo Mbeki, and so in 1997 Ramaphosa left politics to go into business….big business as he eventually became one of South Africa’s richest men…..Then in 201 he was elected Deputy President.

James: When Cyril was approached now you will deputise this man…organization.

Bongani: The first real stain on his image must surely be Marikana, fairly or unfairly?
Prof Mcebisi Ndletyana : Part of the anger against Cyril is that he’s part of mining industry that has not offered any reparations for deliberating impoverishment of rural areas in this country that’s the thing he still might have to make up for. But do you blame him directly for the massacre it would be extremely unfair to single him out for a blame for that massacre specifically because their was a lot happening there and of course the Min of Police at the time was Nathe Motetwe

V/O
Another sore point against Cyril was his silence on corruption and State Capture in his years as Zuma’s Deputy.

RAY I think he doesn’t like to confront difficult challenges until he is sure the playing field is tilted in his favour so for many years he was at JZ side patting him on the back , defending him because he believed that in the party he didn’t have the backing to take Zuma on successfully and to do so would have isolated him so he waited until the moment when he did have that in late 2017 and then he went out on the offensive.

LINK
The man with many faces, the Trade Unionist the skilled negotiator, he over saw the process that gave us the constitution, he’s a capitalist, businessman…who is CR? It would appear that he morphs into any role that is required of him and now he is going to have to bring all of them into the presidency with him

Ray If you want to know what he stands for look at constitution today, he was very very firm on the Bill of Rights on the need for human rights to be at the centre of the constitution and on the openness, transparency and the kind of society that he was bringing into being I think that’s where he showed you his true values.

V/O 8 and a half
For most South Africans, Friday evening signaled a brand new dawn -in our new Presidents words - but how must things change.

FRANK The challenges is that that it’s comrades against comrades and it’s comrades who don’t believe in a just society, they believe in a society where you loot the state to benefit the few and that’s where he is going to have the greatest difficulty.

RAY: I think he has to do something quiet dramatic to persuade the ANC’s base that the party is getting somewhere on transformation in the society In an ironic way he has to prove himself not to be the tool of white monopoly capital in a way that Zuma didn’t necessarily have to.

Bongani: Do we have the chance to regain the optimism the faith that was once placed on South Africa?
M It is the moment Cyril is closely associated with Mandela so it’s easy to recreate a reinvention of the Mandela moment and his language his demeanor lends him to recapture that moment of optimism.
Bongani: And yet we are a very different country from 2019 to 1994//you can’t sell rainbowism as easily as Mandela did today?
M : Rainbowism is not fashionable anymore part of the reason you have racial tension, why you have the rise of the EFF is partly because the politics of reconciliation have run their course. I think we are looking for address but in pressing the case for address you need to be smart about it you do need a figure that is not instilling fear in people you need to invite people on to the table/// I think Cyril is that kind of a person and because of his background because of the suspicion he is a creation of white capital he knows that he has to push quiet hard on that front and white establishment will attach a lot of credence to Cyril saying that they trust him///.
Bongani: He is the man of the moment.
M : He is the man of the moment, he deserves the job and most importantly he has all the qualifications for the job.
